clue.text: Food: goes off-it is the insects.

parts.note: butter is a food spread on bread
to go off quickly, to depart in a hurry, is to fly; he flies, she goes off

explanation.surface: A warning that some food has spoiled and the insects are to blame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes off' suggests food turning bad, but here it means leaves in a hurry; 'it is the' is linking padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Butterflies are a large group of winged insects with scaly, colourful wings.

clue.text: Not fitting? Girl must take exercise

parts.note: Una is a girl's name
PT is physical training, school exercise

explanation.surface: A girl who is out of shape is told she must take some exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Unapt means unsuitable, not appropriate for the purpose.

clue.text: May hold a service in the afternoon

definitions.text: May hold a service in the afternoon

parts.words: May hold a service in the afternoon
parts.note: reads like a church service held later in the day, but the service is a set of cups and pot carried at teatime

explanation.surface: A notice that a church may hold a service in the afternoon.
explanation.definitionFit: A tray carries the cups, saucers and pot, a tea service, for afternoon tea.

clue.text: Holds bits and pieces but isn't big enough for garbage

definitions.text: Holds bits and pieces but isn't big enough for garbage

parts.words: Holds bits and pieces but isn't big enough for garbage
parts.note: a sack of oddments that is too small for rubbish; its letters are those of the rubbish word with one letter missing

explanation.surface: A small bag good for odds and ends but too small for the rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the answer's letters are the word 'garbage' short of its E and jumbled: literally not big enough to spell it.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragbag is a bag for scraps of cloth, and so any jumbled collection of oddments.

clue.text: The early. variety is tough-skinned

indicators.note: a variety of the words, a different version of them, signals that their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An early kind of fruit or vegetable is said to have a tough skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Leathery describes a hide or skin that is hard and tough like tanned leather.

clue.text: Flags? Topping ginseng's possibly the answer

indicators.note: possibly says the remaining letters might be arranged some other way
topping means cutting off the top, so the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: ginseng's read as a plural word

explanation.surface: If you are flagging, a dose of ginseng might be the remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topping' removes the G from GINSENGS, leaving INSENGS, which 'possibly' rearranges. 'Flags' tempts as a verb meaning tires; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Ensigns are flags, especially those flown by ships to show nationality.

clue.text: Resolution that people won't be making more than once

definitions.text: Resolution that people won't be making more than once

parts.words: Resolution that people won't be making more than once
parts.note: suggests New Year resolutions abandoned, but means a choice so deadly that the chooser never gets to make another

explanation.surface: A grumble that people never keep a resolution beyond the first attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: A decision that leads to death or ruin can by its nature only be made once.

clue.text: Tore round about dire forecast

indicators.note: round says one set of letters is wrapped around the other here

parts.note: fell, as in 'one fell swoop', means cruel or dreadful

indicators.note: about means the word is turned about, its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone rips around in a panic about a terrible forecast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tore round' reads as rushing about; 'about' actually jumbles the word into ORET, and 'round' wraps the old word for cruel around it.
explanation.definitionFit: To foretell is to predict, to forecast what will happen.

clue.text: Check for building material needing extra strength

parts.note: to rein in is to check, restrain
taken as written
cement is a material used in building

explanation.surface: A builder checks a material that needs to be extra strong.
explanation.definitionFit: Reinforcement is added support, something that gives a structure more strength.

clue.text: Drag a mangrove swamp-its habitat

indicators.note: swamp means engulf, so the letters are swallowed up within the words before

explanation.surface: Drag a mangrove swamp and you will find this creature living there.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: the agama is a lizard you might find by dragging such a swamp, and 'swamp' also swallows its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An agama is an Old World lizard, a reptile of tropical regions.

clue.text: Statesman pleased to receive a gem'

parts.note: glad means pleased
a gem is a precious stone

explanation.surface: A politician delighted to be presented with a jewel.
explanation.definitionFit: William Gladstone was a Victorian British Liberal prime minister, four times in office.

clue.text: Fatter ham. dished out with second cutting

indicators.note: food dished out is served up and spread around, so the letters are scattered anew

explanation.surface: Plump ham is served out alongside a second slice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second cutting' looks like more ham being carved; it is the farming sense of a second crop of grass mown after the first.
explanation.definitionFit: An aftermath was originally a second mowing of grass in a season, before its wider meaning of consequences.

clue.text: Information put around about part of the course

indicators.note: put around says one piece is wrapped around the other

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Information is spread about some part of a course of study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put around' looks like spreading gossip, but it is a container signal. The course is a golf course, not a course of study.
explanation.definitionFit: On a golf course the green is the smooth grass area surrounding the hole.

clue.text: Declines in prosperity for, a time, in the City of London

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other here

parts.note: days, as in 'salad days' or 'one's palmy days', can mean a time of prosperity
EC is the postcode area of the City of London

explanation.surface: Businesses decline after a spell of prosperity in the financial district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal. The City is London's financial district, whose postcodes begin with those two letters, and 'days' as in 'better days' means a prosperous spell.
explanation.definitionFit: To decay is to deteriorate or go into decline.

clue.text: Many too advanced in years to get insurance protection

parts.note: C, the Roman numeral for a hundred, stands for many
overage means too old

explanation.surface: Many people are too old to get insurance cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Coverage is the extent of protection an insurance policy gives.

clue.text: Shakespearian 'character seen to thrive. on nothing

parts.note: to prosper is to thrive
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare character who manages to thrive on nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link placing the O after the verb; 'seen to' is padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Prospero is the exiled magician duke at the centre of The Tempest.

clue.text: Communist heart-throb embraced then: spurned

indicators.note: embraced says one piece holds the other in its arms

parts.note: red is a common label for a Communist
a pulse is the throb of the heart

explanation.surface: A Communist hugged a dreamy lover, who then rejected him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart-throb' suggests an idol; it is literally the beat felt at the wrist.
explanation.definitionFit: Repulsed means rebuffed or rejected, driven back.

clue.text: Is active, dealing with them, by gum!.

definitions.text: Is active, dealing with them, by gum!

indicators.note: dealing with the letters means sorting them out, rearranging them

explanation.surface: A dentist keeps busy treating holes in teeth, by gum.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: a dentist is active dealing with these holes beside the gum, and 'by gum!' doubles as a northern English exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Cavities are holes in teeth caused by decay, filled by a dentist.

clue.text: Acquiring the skill to aim the 'gun with ease, say?

definitions.note: a phrase for someone learning; the answer is the noun for such a person

parts.note: to train a gun is to aim it

indicators.note: say means as spoken, signalling a word that sounds like letters

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like EE

explanation.surface: A recruit learning to aim the gun easily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ease' spoken sounds like 'E's', two Es. The definition is loose: a trainee is one acquiring the skill.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainee is a learner, someone being taught a job or craft.

clue.text: Pungent flavouring in rock the Italian brought back

indicators.note: brought back says the whole assembly is read backwards
in places one piece inside the other here

parts.note: a crag is a steep rock
il is Italian for 'the'

explanation.surface: A strong seasoning found by a rock and carried home by an Italian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' builds CILRAG, which 'brought back' then reads in reverse; 'rock' looks like a place where garlic grows, but it is a crag.
explanation.definitionFit: Garlic is a strongly scented bulb used to season food.

clue.text: Immediately following ar rival,..sets out-then stops

indicators.note: immediately following places the next piece straight after the first

parts.note: arr is the abbreviation for arrival on timetables

indicators.note: out means jumbled, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone arrives, sets off at once, then halts.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue as printed splits 'arrival' in two. 'out' rearranges the word into ESTS, and 'Immediately following' places that straight after the timetable abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrest is to halt or stop something.

clue.text: Rents rising over a pound: costs tend to do so, nowadays

definitions.text: costs tend to do so, nowadays

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: rents are tears, rips
L is the abbreviation for pound (libra)

explanation.surface: Rents going up beyond a pound, since prices keep climbing these days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rents' looks like housing costs; it means tears. 'over' sets these letters above the rest in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Prices that spiral climb ever faster, rising in a continuing upward twist.

clue.text: Ayr is in this part of the world

indicators.note: in is taken loosely to signal the letters sit jumbled within the answer

explanation.surface: The Scottish town of Ayr is in this region of the globe.
explanation.walkthrough: Ayr is a town in Scotland; its letters plus IS rearrange to a Middle Eastern country, a mismatch the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: Syria is a country in the Middle East, a region of the world.

clue.text: Superior accommodation in, a garret

parts.note: upper means higher, superior
a room is accommodation

explanation.surface: First-class lodgings to be had in an attic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Superior accommodation' sounds like luxury; it just means a room upstairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A garret is an attic room at the top of a house.

clue.text: You need witchcraft to be a healer — to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: To become a healer you need some witchcraft.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'You need witchcraft' as the definition, but 'You need' is linking: only 'witchcraft' means the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeah is a form of folk magic or sorcery practised in the Caribbean.

clue.text: Filofax containing ring and broken earrings

parts.note: O is ring-shaped

indicators.note: broken says the word is smashed up and its letters reassembled

explanation.surface: A personal planner with a ring binder and some broken jewellery inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' and 'earrings' both suggest jewellery; the ring is just an O. A Filofax is a ring-bound personal planner.
explanation.definitionFit: A personal organiser is a pocket diary and address book, of which Filofax is a brand.

clue.text: Hide 'a note inside the yarn.

indicators.note: inside places the note within the other word

parts.note: a hide is an animal skin
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Concealing a message inside a ball of yarn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb, conceal; it is the noun, skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A skein is a loosely coiled length of yarn or thread.

clue.text: Repair buckled. shoes left in afternoon by. musician

annotationWithheld.why: Repair buckled. shoes left in afternoon by. musician: MEND + shoes jumbled round L gives MENDELSSOH, but nothing in 'afternoon by' accounts for the final N
annotationWithheld.clue: Repair buckled. shoes left in afternoon by. musician
